warmup.text: This is the last day of the week. In Chapter 19, Isaac learns what he can and cannot do as a ghost, and he goes looking for Naomi. The poem today asks the same question twice. Notice how you can know something is there, even when you cannot see it.

words.text: Last day with the sight roots. Explain the difference between looking and seeing. Then the academic pairs that trip up even grown writers: affect and effect, principal and principle. Then the last five words in the spyglass.

reading.text: Read Chapter 19 in your book. Watch what Isaac discovers in the soldiers' camp, and listen to what Naomi says when he whispers her name. Then put the week together with your lens: name the theme. Finish with the Virtue Watch at the end of this tab.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 19, then your final revised story: five to seven sentences with at least one detail you can sense and one comparison. Then one sentence about what imagery adds. Copy your work and paste it into Canvas.

Find the line or picture that comes back.
Read Think About It and keep your answer in mind.
how.why: When a poet repeats something, each new picture adds to the idea. That is how a theme grows.

how.why: Explaining two close words out loud shows you know them.

how.why: Using a word in your own sentence is the best proof you know it.

how.why: Mixing short and long sentences controls where a reader slows down.

glossary.meaning: to put ideas from different parts together into one bigger idea

miss.affect: To affect is to change or influence. It is an action (a verb).
miss.effect: An effect is a result. It names a thing (a noun).
miss.principal: A principal is the chief or head of something.
miss.principle: A principle is a rule or belief. It names a thing.

game.title: The Spyglass
game.sub: This week's word game · 5 words today
game.look: Isaac sees what other people cannot see. In this game, a brass spyglass looks at one word at a time. First tap the root hiding inside it: vis or vid means see, and spect means look. The root lights up. Then tap what the word means. Every word you get adds a star to the spyglass.

do: Look at the word in the spyglass.
Tap the root you find inside it.
Tap what the word means.
Tap Next word.
how.why: If you can spot a root, you can work out a long word you have never seen.

game.doneLine: That is the whole week's sky. Well done.

art.title: Moonlight
art.alt: A dark painting of trees against a glowing moonlit sky, with moonlight on still water.
art.look: Ralph Albert Blakelock painted this moonlit night around 1885 to 1890. It is not Isaac's road, but it feels like Chapter 19: night by the river, the soldiers' fire burning low, and frogs calling from the water.

virtue.intro: Look back at Chapters 16 to 19. Tap the moment you think shows courage the most.

Joseph fights the wolf to save Isaac.
